text: The purpose of this document is to assist Cadence in understanding and operationalizing the enhancements made to its Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) capabilities through the implementation of the OneTrust TPRM solution. This engagement aims to provide Cadence with a standardized, scalable, and automated solution that aligns with its business, operational, and compliance requirements. l
As part of this engagement, Optiv supported the implementation and configuration of Cadence’s OneTrust TPRM instance. This comprises:
Designing and implementing structured workflows aligned with Cadence’s operational needs and TPRM requirements.
Configuring user roles to ensure appropriate access management.
Establishing vendor onboarding attributes to streamline supplier risk processes.
Refreshing and tailoring the Due Diligence Questionnaire to ensure alignment with Cadence’s risk assessment objectives and regulatory requirements.
Through this effort, Cadence will attain a more structured, transparent, and efficient TPRM framework, reducing manual effort and ensuring compliance with internal and external risk requirements.

The scope of this document focuses on Cadence’s TPRM processes, and the responsibilities of internal stakeholders involved in managing third-party risks. The following activities are included within this scope:

Current State Analysis: Review the current state of Cadence’s OneTrust TPRM instance, including its configuration, workflows, and supporting processes, while also assessing alignment with the broader TPRM program.
Refreshing the Due Diligence Questionnaire: Enhance and update existing questionnaires to align with Cadence’s organizational structure, compliance needs, and industry best practices.
Configuration of OneTrust TPRM: Document and configure custom workflows, rules, questionnaire templates, and notification processes in OneTrust tailored to Cadence’s requirements.

Training & Knowledge Transfer: Provide documentation covering OneTrust setup and configuration, workflow logics and questionnaire rules, ensuring Cadence stakeholders can effectively manage and operate the solution.

Currently, Cadence’s TPRM program is positioned at the “Siloed Risk Function” stage, where risk ownership and assessment activities are distributed across functions such as Legal, Compliance, Security, and Procurement. Each area maintains its own risk processes, resulting in fragmented oversight.

The strategic objective of this engagement is to transition Cadence toward the “Integrated Risk Management (IRM)” stage - where all third-party risks are collectively managed through a unified, automated, and standardized framework within OneTrust. This will establish a single source of truth for vendor risk visibility, governance, and decision-making.
A key enabler of this transformation is the integration between Ironclad and OneTrust, which connects contract lifecycle management with third-party risk workflows. Through this integration:
Contract creation and execution in Ironclad automatically triggers corresponding due diligence and assessment workflows in OneTrust.
Vendor-related data (e.g., contract terms, renewal dates, risk tier, and compliance status) synchronizes between systems for continuous visibility.
Risk and contractual obligations are managed cohesively within a single ecosystem.
Optiv’s implementation approach supports this evolution by consolidating all risk-related processes into OneTrust and aligning them with two primary risk domains:

Identified through due diligence questionnaires covering Legal, Financial, Privacy, and Compliance areas. These assessments capture vendor-level dependencies, regulatory exposures, and process inefficiencies at both organizational and product/service levels.
Identified through security questionnaires focusing on data protection, access control, incident management, and infrastructure security.
By structuring risk assessments around these two domains, and integrating Ironclad with OneTrust, Cadence can now:
Manage operational and cybersecurity risks in a unified workstream.
Automate due diligence, escalation, and remediation workflows.
Maintain cross-functional visibility across all risk stakeholders.
Strengthen accountability through consistent, platform-driven governance.
Progress toward a mature Integrated Risk Management model that aligns risk oversight with Cadence’s business objectives and growth strategy.

Cadence’s third-party workflows in OneTrust are now fully automated and tailored to the criticality and type of vendor.

Third parties are classified based on data sensitivity and risk criticality, with separate workflows established for Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 vendors. Tier 3 third parties typically represent lower-risk engagements (e.g., limited data access or short-term service contracts), while Tiers 1 and 2 represent medium- and high-risk third parties requiring enhanced due diligence.

Additionally, classification by third-party Category ensures that distinct workflows are automatically triggered for Staffing Vendors, Service Providers, Marketing Partners, Revenue Partners, and International Vendors.

When a new third-party is added to the OneTrust platform, it is routed through an automated onboarding workflow that analyzes both third-party tier and category. Based on these attributes, the system assigns the appropriate workflow path for due diligence, assessment, and approval.

Cadence’s OneTrust environment has been configured with automated workflows that manage the lifecycle of third-party assessments based on both vendor category and risk tier. The integration between Ironclad and OneTrust ensures that every new vendor entering the system is automatically analyzed and assigned to the appropriate workflow.

Update questions, sections, or logic rules as required.
Save and validate the new version with the Vendor Risk Management team before publishing.

Open the existing published questionnaire template.
Make changes in questions and rules

Cadence Financial Group, Inc. (the “Group") accepts risk as an inherent consequence of providing investment banking, asset
management and consumer banking services. This policy establishes the Group-wide framework through which risk is identified,
assessed, treated, monitored and reported, so that risk-taking is deliberate, understood, and remains within the appetite set by the
Board of Directors.

This policy is the apex document of the Group risk policy hierarchy. All subordinate risk policies, standards and procedures must be
consistent with it. Where a subordinate document conflicts with this policy, this policy prevails. Interpretation questions are directed to
the policy author, Tobias Lindqvist (t.lindqvist@cadencefg.com, +44 20 7555 0171).

1. Protect capital, liquidity and earnings by ensuring exposures remain within approved appetite and regulatory limits.
2. Enable informed risk-taking through a consistent, comparable view of risk across business lines and geographies.
3. Establish clear accountability for every material risk, with a single named owner at an appropriate level of seniority.
4. Ensure regulatory compliance with prudential, conduct and data-protection obligations in each jurisdiction.
5. Protect customers and market integrity by embedding conduct considerations into risk decisions.
6. Safeguard reputation by identifying and managing risks to stakeholder confidence.

7, Support resilience so the Group can absorb severe but plausible shocks and continue important business services,
8. Promote a healthy risk culture in which concerns are raised early, escalated without fear, and acted upon.

Risk ownership Risk is owned by the business that creates it. Ownership cannot be delegated to a control function or to a third party.
Proportionality The depth of assessment, control and reporting is proportionate to the materiality and complexity of the risk.
Independence The second and third lines have direct, unrestricted access to the Board and are free from business pressure.
Transparency Risks are reported completely and without filtering. Understating or delaying a risk report is a breach of this policy.
Forward focus The framework considers emerging and prospective risks, not only realised losses and historical events.
Consistency Acommon taxonomy, scoring scale and definitions apply Group-wide so that risks aggregate meaningfully.
Substance over form Assessments reflect actual exposure and actual control operation, not documented intent.

This policy applies to Cadence Financial Group, Inc. and every subsidiary, branch and representative office it controls, including
regulated entities in the United States, the United Kingdom, the European Union, India, Singapore and Hong Kong. Where a subsidiary
is subject to a local requirement more stringent than this policy, the local requirement applies and the divergence is recorded in the
Group Policy Divergence Register maintained by Delphine R. Okonjo (d.okonjo@cadencefg.com).

Joint ventures and associates in which the Group does not hold control are out of scope. The Group's interest in such entities is
managed as an investment exposure under the Credit Risk Policy and as a reputational exposure under this policy.

This policy applies to all directors, employees, secondees, contingent workers and contractors acting for the Group, regardless of
location or employment status. Third parties performing outsourced activities are bound through contractual terms requiring equivalence
with this policy, per Section 18.3.

18. Change, new product and third-party risk

Change is a significant source of operational risk. All material change initiatives — system implementations, migrations, organisational
restructures, outsourcing transitions and regulatory implementation programmes — require a risk assessment at initiation, at each major
stage gate and prior to go-live. The assessment must address risks introduced by the change, risks to business-as-usual during
transition, control coverage during parallel running, and the rollback position if the change fails.

Go-live approval requires confirmation that controls have been designed, implemented and tested; that data migration has been
reconciled; that affected staff have been trained; that support arrangements are in place; and that a documented rollback plan exists.
Go-live may not proceed on the basis that controls will be implemented shortly afterwards.

No new product, service, market or distribution channel may be launched without approval from the New Product Approval Committee,
chaired by Priyanka S. Raghavan. A material change to an existing product requires the same approval. The submission must address,
at minimum: target market, customer need and foreseeable harm; risk assessment across every applicable taxonomy category; legal,
regulatory, tax and accounting analysis; financial crime, sanctions and conduct assessment, a data privacy impact assessment where
personal data is processed; technology, resilience and third-party dependencies; operational readiness; pricing, profitability and capital
consumption; and exit and wind-down arrangements.

Every approved product is subject to post-implementation review within twelve months, assessing whether the product performed as
expected, whether customer outcomes matched those anticipated, and whether the risk assessment remains valid.

Third-party arrangements are managed across the full lifecycle: strategy and sourcing, due diligence, contracting, onboarding, ongoing
monitoring and exit. Depth of oversight is determined by criticality tier, assessed on the importance of the service, the sensitivity of data
